synopsis: ISO 16001:2017 sets performance and test requirements for object-detection systems and visibility aids; the booklet dates it to November 2017, reports confirmation in 2023, and emphasizes that it covers warning and visibility, not braking [f6744, f2181]. It is the only off-road standard found with hard detection and warning numbers: detection within 300 ms, audible warnings at least 3 dB above ambient, and a flashing red light for the most severe warning, alongside continuous self-checking and no single-action disablement [f160, f2064, f2065, f2066, f2067, f2068]. Its framework defines a test body, detection zone and detection time, with physical-test procedures and technology annexes that lack a dedicated lidar annex [f5354, f11232, f2069]. For virtual validation, the corpus uses its detection limit in physics parameterisation and its visibility-type methods for geometric blind-zone analysis, but reports no simulation-credibility acceptance rules and no evidence establishing acceptance of simulation evidence [f7493, f11549, f5110, f11237]. Planners should confirm the 300 ms limit against the purchased standard before safety-case use: it was sourced from a public preview rather than verified against the full standard, while other chapters also flag unverified editions, dates and simulation clauses [f7493, f7494, f7495, f4335, f5111].
